transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up an appointment from someone who really needs it, but... I guess I've just been a little stressed lately? Is that okay to talk about here? 

It's just that my mind is constantly jumping around. It's probably silly, and I know I should handle it better, but I just keep worrying about work—like whether our lab's new partnership is going to cut my position, or if the data I'm running is all wrong. And then it just kind of snowballs into worrying about my bills piling up, and how my family probably thinks I'm falling behind... and whether I've already completely ruined my chances at getting into grad school. 

I'm sure everyone deals with this kind of stuff, but it's just a lot of thoughts at once. Does that make sense?
Have you been avoiding any situations or activities because of these worries?

No, no, I don't think I've been avoiding anything. I mean, I still go to the lab every day, and I try to keep up with my friends when they invite me out. I really don't want to be that guy who just flakes on everyone, you know? So I push through it. I mean, sometimes I might, like, take a little longer to reply to an email because I want to make sure it sounds perfectly okay, but I wouldn't call that avoiding. That's just being careful, right? I try really hard to just do everything I'm supposed to do. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Have you noticed any changes in your body, like headaches or difficulty sleeping, when you're feeling overwhelmed by these worries?

Well, um, I guess I do get some headaches. But it's probably just from staring at the computer screen too much, you know? I mean, I try to have good posture, but I catch myself clenching my jaw a lot when I'm looking over spreadsheets. 

And, um, my shoulders and neck get pretty tight during the day. By the time I get home, I feel this stiffness... kind of like I've been carrying heavy lab equipment around all day, even when I haven't. But I'm sure that's just normal stress, right? A lot of people get tense at work. I just need to remember to stretch more, probably. Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty. I'm actually really lucky, you know? I have a job in a lab, I have friends... I try to stay positive about things. 

Sure, I get a little overwhelmed with all the worrying, but I'm not depressed or anything like that. I still care about my work and I still want to do well. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or feeling sorry for myself, because I'm definitely not. I'm just... trying to figure out how to manage my thoughts better. Is it okay that I don't feel sad? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you worry about being judged or evaluated by others?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I care about doing a good job, obviously. But I wouldn't say I'm, like, paranoid about people judging me. 

I just... I want to be a good employee and a good friend. So, yeah, I guess I think about how I'm coming across, but that's just being considerate, isn't it? Like, I want to make sure my lab reports are accurate so my supervisor doesn't have to correct them. It's not that I'm scared of her evaluating me, I just want to be helpful and do things right the first time. I don't think that's a bad thing, right? Wanting to do a good job?
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Um, no, not like that. I mean, I definitely think about things a lot, especially work stuff or making sure I didn't forget to pay a bill, but it's not like I'm stuck on some weird thought I can't shake. 

I just... I like to be thorough, you know? So if I'm thinking about a conversation I had or a project at the lab, it's just me trying to make sure I handled it the right way. It's just normal problem-solving, I think. I don't have, like, crazy thoughts taking over my brain or anything. I can focus on other things when I need to. That makes sense, right? I'm just a bit of an over-thinker sometimes, but nothing extreme.
Do you feel like you're thinking about things over and over even when you don't want to?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try my best to just focus on one thing at a time. Like, I'll tell myself to just concentrate on finishing a report or checking an assay at the lab. I always want to be productive, you know? 

But sometimes... I guess one little concern just kind of sets off another one. And then pretty soon I'm just staring at the screen, and my head is running through every possible way things could go wrong. I know I shouldn't do it, and I really try to snap out of it so I can get back to my work. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or anything... I always get my tasks done eventually. It's just a little hard to turn the worrying off sometimes, even when I really want to. Is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
Do you feel like any of your thoughts are intrusive or unwelcome?

Um, no, I wouldn't use words like "intrusive" or "unwelcome." That sounds kind of... intense, I guess? Like I'm losing control or something, and I'm really not. 

I just have a lot on my plate, you know, with the lab and everything. So if a thought pops up about an experiment I'm running or a deadline I have, it's just my brain trying to keep me organized. It's not unwelcome, it's actually kind of helpful, right? Because it keeps me on top of things. I'd hate to be the kind of person who just forgets important details. So, yeah, I definitely don't have intrusive thoughts. I'm just being responsible... I think that's normal, isn't it?
Do you feel like you have to repeat certain actions or rituals to feel okay or to prevent something bad from happening?

Um, no, definitely not. I don't do anything like that. I know some people have to, like, wash their hands a certain number of times or check the stove over and over, but I don't do any of those things. 

I mean, I double-check my work at the lab, of course. Like, I'll make sure the equipment is calibrated right or that I logged my data correctly. But that's just being professional, right? You have to be precise in chemistry. I don't do it because I'm scared something terrible will happen, I just... I just want to do a good job and not make mistakes. That's just being thorough, isn't it? I definitely don't have any rituals or anything like that. I'm doing okay, right?
Do you ever feel a strong urge to perform a specific behavior over and over?

Um, no, not at all. I don't get urges like that. I mean, I like to be thorough, like I said, but I don't feel forced to do anything over and over. 

I really just try to be a good employee and make sure my work is accurate. I don't have any strange habits or anything that would get in the way of my job. I'm pretty normal in that regard, you know? I just want to make sure I'm doing things right. That's a good thing, isn't it?
Do you feel like there are specific things you need to do in a specific way to feel comfortable or to reduce your anxiety?

Um, no, not really. I don't have, like, a rigid routine or anything I *have* to do to feel okay. I mean, I like things to be organized, especially at work. I usually set up my workstation the same way before I start a new synthesis, just so I know where everything is. But that's just being efficient, right? 

I don't do it because I'm anxious, I just do it because it makes sense. It helps me focus on the chemistry instead of looking for a beaker or whatever. I can totally be flexible if I need to be. I don't have any weird quirks or anything that would make me hard to work with. I'm just trying to be a good scientist, you know? That's what you're supposed to do, isn't it?
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your daily life or relationships?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, I wouldn't say it's *interfering*, exactly. I'm still getting by, mostly. But... I did, um, I missed an internal deadline at the lab recently. It wasn't a huge deal, I just... I couldn't seem to get my writing organized, and reviewing the data just felt so overwhelming. I just wanted it to be perfect, you know? 

And lately, I don't know, it just feels like everything takes so much energy. Even just routine stuff, like putting together reports for work, or... or showing up for the art nights I usually go to. Even cooking for my family just feels like... like it's too much to keep up with right now. But everyone gets overwhelmed sometimes, right? It's just a busy season. I'm sure I'll get back on track soon. That's pretty normal for someone my age, trying to build a career, isn't it?
How long have you been experiencing these worries?

Um, let's see... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe about... seven months? Give or take? 

It kind of started right around the time our lab had this big funding shift. We entered into a new commercial partnership, and it basically changed how everything was being run day-to-day. So, you know, there were a lot of new expectations and shifting protocols to learn. 

Anyone would be a little stressed trying to adapt to all that, right? I'm really just trying to make sure I'm keeping up with the new standards and doing a good job for the new partners. It's completely normal to take a few months to adjust to a big structural change like that, isn't it?
Have you been experiencing these worries for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past seven months?

Um... well, "most of the day" sounds a bit extreme, doesn't it? I mean, I'm working, I'm doing things. I'm not just sitting around worrying all day. I'm productive. 

But, I guess... it's always kind of there? Like, in the background. Even when I'm focused on a synthesis, there's this little voice reminding me about the new protocols or what the partners might think of the results. And yeah, I suppose it's been pretty consistent since the funding shift. So... nearly every day, maybe. But that's just because work has been so demanding every day, you know? It's just me trying to stay on top of things. That's a good quality for a scientist to have, right? Being attentive to the details?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to enjoy activities you used to find pleasurable since the worrying started?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still really like doing the things I usually do. Like... when I actually get to those art nights I mentioned earlier, I still think they're really fun. 

I guess, um, maybe I just haven't been doing them quite as much lately, but that's really just because I'm trying to be responsible and prioritize the lab work right now. I want to make sure I'm not letting anyone down. But the enjoyment is definitely still there when I do have a free moment. That's a good sign, isn't it? Like, it shows I'm still keeping a positive attitude about things, right?
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you significant distress or interfering with your ability to function in your daily life?

Um, well... I wouldn't use a strong word like "interfering," really. I'm still showing up every day and putting in the effort. I'm trying my best, you know? 

But, um... I guess things have been a little harder to juggle lately. Just... keeping all the plates spinning. Like, I did actually miss an internal deadline at the lab recently. It wasn't a huge deal, I don't think, but I just... I couldn't seem to get my writing and the data review organized the way I usually do. My mind was just kind of spinning with all the new partner expectations. 

And, um, I guess outside of work, things have slipped a little bit too. Like those art nights... I haven't really been showing up for them. And even just normal things, like cooking for my family, it just... it feels like a lot to manage right now. Like it's just too much to keep up with on top of everything else. 

But that's just because I care so much about doing a good job at work, right? It makes sense that I'd be a little overwhelmed when I'm putting so much energy into the lab. That doesn't mean I'm failing at everything else, does it? I'm just prioritizing, right?
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of emotional pain or discomfort?

Um... emotional pain? That sounds... really intense. I wouldn't say "pain." I mean, I'm not, like, crying all the time or falling apart. I'm holding it together. 

It's just... maybe more like a lot of discomfort? Or just... tension. It's exhausting, honestly, always trying to anticipate what could go wrong with the protocols or what the partners need. Sometimes my chest feels really tight, and I just feel... worn out. But I'm just trying to be thorough and responsible. It's normal to feel a little stressed when you care about your work, right? I'm sure you see a lot of people who get a bit overwhelmed when they're trying to do their best... right?
Do you feel like you have to do things in a very specific way to feel right?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't have any weird rituals or anything like that, if that's what you mean. 

I do like things to be organized, especially at the lab. You know, making sure the equipment is calibrated and the samples are labeled correctly. But that's just being a good chemist, right? You have to be precise in this field, otherwise, the data is useless. 

So, I guess I have a routine for how I set up my bench, but it's not like... I don't feel like something terrible will happen if I don't do it exactly the same way. It's just more efficient, you know? I'm just trying to be professional and do a good job. That's a pretty normal way to work, isn't it? Being careful and detail-oriented is a good trait to have, right?
Have you noticed any significant problems at work or in your relationships due to your worrying?

Um... well, like I mentioned before, I did miss that one internal deadline at the lab. It was just because I couldn't quite get my writing and the data review organized the way I usually do. But it really wasn't a huge disaster or anything, just a little slip-up. 

And, um, I guess I have noticed that some other things are feeling a bit harder to manage lately. Like, even just routine stuff at work, like preparing the regular reports... it just takes a bit more out of me right now. And, you know, I mentioned the art nights with my friends, how I haven't been going to those. And even just cooking for my family at home... it all just feels like a little too much to keep up with sometimes. 

But I think that's just because I'm so focused on making sure the lab work is perfect, you know? It's natural that some other things might take a backseat when you're really dedicated to your career, right? I'm not, like, completely falling apart at work or anything. I'm still doing my best to be a good employee and a good family member... that's what matters most, right?
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships with friends or family due to your worrying?

Um... no, not really. I mean, my family is great, and my friends are really understanding. 

I guess, like I said, I haven't been going to the art nights, but my friends know I'm just really busy with the lab right now. They get it. And with my family... I mean, I might be a little more quiet at home sometimes, or maybe I don't cook as much as I used to, but we're all fine. We still watch TV together and everything. 

I try really hard not to let my stress affect them, you know? I don't want to be a burden or complain all the time. I think I do a pretty good job of keeping it to myself so it doesn't cause any real friction. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just trying to keep the peace and not make a big deal out of things... right?
